feature: Trust-data hardening for Discipulado IEADPE internal mode
global_constraints: User-facing copy uses pt-BR; identifiers, code, specifications, and technical documentation use English.
The app runs on Firebase Spark with no Cloud Functions; authorization is enforced only by firestore.rules.
Do not deploy, push, import legacy data, or send messages. Emulator verification is the release evidence.
Use stable opaque IDs, ISO date-only strings for calendar dates, UTC server timestamps, integer revisions starting at 1.
Each touches entry is an exact production/configuration/documentation path exclusively owned by that task. Tasks with overlapping touches never share a wave.
No expected_red field. RED tests are authored just-in-time by the operator; acceptance and spec_refs travel with each task.
No Admin SDK keys or privileged credentials in browser-served code. No PII in logs, URLs, or error reports.

tasks.title: Lock NFR drivers and accepted-race runbook
tasks.summary: Record security-first NFR drivers and the operator runbook for advisory uniqueness, enrollment-cap race, and paging cost. This is the sole owner of the trust-data NFR doc consumed by tasks 2-4.
acceptance: docs/trust-data-nfr.md ranks security above availability above performance with one paragraph of rationale per driver tied to Spark client-write mode.
The doc lists each relaxed invariant (advisory name uniqueness, best-effort enrollment cap, no counters, client paging amplification) with accepted behavior plus numbered operator resolution steps.
No code, rules, or handler file is modified in this task.

tasks.title: Re-harden Firestore rules and indexes
tasks.summary: Remove the hardcoded owner email, audit scoped grants for activeEnrollmentRefs and class/session roster paths, and pin required composite indexes. Sole owner of rules and indexes in this plan.
acceptance: firestore.rules contains no hardcoded personal email; the allowlist credential is a clearly marked placeholder with a rotation procedure referenced from docs/trust-data-nfr.md.

congregations/{id}/activeEnrollmentRefs/{refId}, classes/{classId}/roster/{rosterId}, and sessions/{sessionId}/roster/{rosterId} are explicitly granted to supervisor plus own-congregation staff and covered by allow/deny cases; every other path falls to the deny catch-all.

firestore.indexes.json declares the shipped directory, student, class, session, and enrollment filter/order combinations; an unsupported combination is rejected in repository input, not silently scanned.
Backend unit compile passes; emulator security suites are updated but their execution evidence belongs to the verification-quality plan, not this task.

tasks.title: Align handler validation and safe errors
tasks.summary: Mirror Dart and TypeScript validation semantics and centralize safe error mapping. Sole owner of the listed handler, validation, and error files in this plan.
acceptance: Name normalization (lowercase, diacritics stripped), Brazilian phone to E.164, birth-date America/Recife range, and nullable baptism semantics behave identically in Dart and TypeScript against shared fixtures.
Mutations carry stable UUID plus expectedRevision and requestId; stale revision returns conflict without overwrite and timeout preserves draft plus retry identity.
SDK and rules denials map to AppFailure codes validation, unauthenticated, forbidden, notFound, conflict, unavailable, unknown with safe pt-BR messages and no stack traces, tokens, or raw payloads.
New unit tests cover accented homonyms, leap-day dates, contradictory baptism answers, stale revision, and idempotent replay with altered-payload rejection.

tasks.title: Bound directory and prefix read cost
tasks.summary: Measure reads per directory and name-prefix page and record the Spark budget. Sole owner of the codec, transport-support, and budget doc in this plan.
acceptance: docs/read-budget.md records measured Firestore reads for one directory page and one global prefix page at 50-record default and states the per-1000-page projection.
query_codec cursors bind scope, filter, and ordering identity and reject reuse after filter or scope change; cursors never appear in public URLs.
No rules or handler file from tasks 2-3 is modified in this task.
